title: Borscht
subtitle: Ukrainian beetroot soup with beef and soured cream
excerpt: The great soup of Eastern Europe: beetroot, beef, cabbage, and vegetables simmered into a deep crimson, sweet-sour broth finished with a spoonful of soured cream. Made in Ukraine, Russia, Poland, and across the region with endless variations, but always built around beetroot.

recipe.sourceNotes: Borscht (borshch in Ukrainian) is one of the defining dishes of Ukrainian cuisine and one of the most complex soups in the Eastern European culinary tradition. Recognised by UNESCO as part of Ukraine's intangible cultural heritage in 2022, it predates the use of beet as its base ingredient; early versions used wild hogweed (borch in old Slavic). The adoption of cultivated beetroot in the seventeenth to eighteenth centuries transformed it into the vivid crimson soup now known worldwide. There are hundreds of regional and family variations: Kyiv borscht uses pork and beans; cold borscht (kholodnyk) is made with kefir and served in summer; beet kvass gives a more fermented flavour. The constant is the beet. Soured cream (smetana in Ukrainian) is the classic finish.

content.text: Add the beetroot in two stages: half cooked into the soup from the beginning for colour and depth, half grated and added at the end with vinegar to preserve the vivid colour. The vinegar is essential for the characteristic sweet-sour balance and for keeping the colour bright; without it the borscht turns brownish. Do not boil vigorously once the late beetroot goes in.

content.text: Put the beef in a large pot and cover with 2 litres of cold water. Bring to the boil, skim the foam, then reduce to a simmer. Add the bay leaves and 1 teaspoon of salt. Simmer for 45 minutes. Add the matchstick beetroot (the first 300 g) and continue simmering for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, fry the onion in oil for 8 minutes until soft. Add the carrot and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes more. Add to the pot along with the cabbage and potato. Simmer for 20 minutes until the potato and cabbage are tender.

Remove the beef and shred the meat, discarding any bones. Return the meat to the pot. Add the grated beetroot (the second 300 g), red wine vinegar, sugar, and remaining salt. Stir well and simmer very gently for 10 minutes; do not boil hard. Taste: the soup should be savoury, sweet, and sour in roughly equal measure. Serve with a generous spoonful of soured cream and scattered dill.
